hypothesis: With the same seed, 300-second budget, data, and evaluation, `WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.1` will process more updates at the peak learning rate and finish with lower `val_bpb` than `0.5`.

experiment_plan.goal: Test whether shortening the learning-rate warmdown from 50% to 10% of the same 300-second training budget improves final `val_bpb` by keeping training at peak learning rates longer.
changes: Make no other changes: retain the existing linear `get_lr_multiplier` decay, `FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.0`, all optimizer learning rates, seed, model, data pipeline, evaluation, and time budget.
Run the modified configuration once under the same conditions as the existing `WARMDOWN_RATIO=0.5` baseline, and compare the existing final `val_bpb` output.
experiment_plan.reasoning: This single hyperparameter change moves the start of linear decay from 50% to 90% training progress, directly isolating the selected hypothesis while preserving the decay shape and endpoint. Holding every other setting fixed maintains comparability; the existing `val_bpb` output is sufficient to determine whether the 10% warmdown finishes better than the 50% baseline.
